issue.title: Are status details always proto?

repository.name: grpc-go
repository.description: The Go language implementation of gRPC. HTTP/2 based RPC

issue.body:
As part of an internal project, I'm looking at using gRPC with non-standard codecs. Some of the legacy software that would interoperate with this gRPC code can't use the open-source gRPC client libraries, so we'd need to write simple clients for unary RPCs on top of an off-the-shelf HTTP/2 client. Most of the resulting work is straightforward, but I'm not sure how to handle error details properly.

From what I can see, the data supporting the [`Status.Details`](https://godoc.org/google.golang.org/grpc/status#Status.Details) and [`Status.WithDetails`](https://godoc.org/google.golang.org/grpc/status#Status.WithDetails) APIs are written to and [read from the wire](https://sourcegraph.com/github.com/grpc/grpc-go@master/-/blob/internal/transport/http_util.go#L317) as a base64-encoded proto blob, following the ["Binary Headers" portion of the HTTP/2 gRPC protocol](https://github.com/grpc/grpc/blob/master/doc/PROTOCOL-HTTP2.md#protocol) (for now, pending the proposal to negotiate non-base64-encoded binary metadata).

Do you intend this data to *always* be proto, even if the request and response of the RPC are using a different codec? If so, is this part of the protocol or an implementation detail? If the former, should this be documented in the protocol spec?

For reference, I'm looking at the grpc-go code on master. This portion of the code doesn't seem to have changed from the 0.15.x branch.

issue.title: Adaptor gRPC Error Messages

repository.name: nitric
repository.description: Nitric is a multi-language framework for cloud applications with infrastructure from code.

issue.body:
It would be very useful for operational support and developer debugging to included contextual information with Membrane Plugin Errors.  Instead of using arbitrarily formatted text error message we would use a JSON error message with a documented schema.

An example error message at the adaptor layer enforcing GRPC validation:

```json
{ 
   "code": "Invalid Argument", 
   "desc": "invalid collection name", 
   "service": "DocumentService.Get", 
   "args": [
      "wiDHZI8Qc0MckP3w$zjQCpuT$g&pR0On", 
      "1h5LvG%$s1GU&9K5EUUn^#RUCSS48Qck"
    ]
}
```

An example error of a plugin service message could be:

```json
{ 
   "code": "Not Found", 
   "desc": "unable to retrieve value", 
   "plugin": "FirestoreDocService.Get", 
   "args": [
      "customers", 
      "peterson@host.com" 
    ]
}
```

With plugin service errors the service adaptor would still be responsible for creating JSON error message from the error information returned by the underlying service.  The plugin would also define `service` or `plugin` name and `args` attributes.

The adaptor layer would take care only to include only non-sensitive service arguments.  This approach will relieve the underlying services from having to implement duplicated error handling code, and will make implementing security practices easier to support. 

The JSON error message would be limited to 1KB in length to ensure compatibility.  If gRPC spec evolves to better support serialized error message, we can modify the adaptor error library to support this:

* https://github.com/grpc/grpc/issues/24007

Having a standardized JSON error message will also enable much better error message display in the Nitric SDKs.



┆Issue is synchronized with this [Clickup task](https://app.clickup.com/t/1dyn945) by [Unito](https://www.unito.io)

issue.title: Add google.rpc.Status-compatible gRPC errors
issue.body:
This PR adds [Status](https://github.com/googleapis/googleapis/blob/master/google/rpc/status.proto)—based errors which are supported by all major gRPC implementations (including Java and Go).

A similar client-side change is needed in Wire to expose the details.

issue.title: Improve error messages by supporting ErrorInfo and AIP-193

labels.name: type: feature request
labels.description: ‘Nice-to-have’ improvement, new feature or different behavior or design.

repository.name: google-cloud-cpp
repository.description: C++ Client Libraries for Google Cloud Services

issue.body:
https://google.aip.dev/193 describes the recommended way for Google services to return additional error information to users. The additional data is sent in the https://github.com/googleapis/api-common-protos/blob/master/google/rpc/status.proto `details` field, which is a **repeated** `google.protobuf.Any`. This is exposed to in C++ via `grpc::Status`'s `.error_details()` method (https://grpc.github.io/grpc/cpp/classgrpc_1_1_status.html), which returns `std::string`. As of today, our [`google::cloud::Status`](https://github.com/googleapis/google-cloud-cpp/blob/main/google/cloud/status.h) class drops the error details on the ground.

So I think we need to do the following:
- [x] Attach "error_details" to [`google::cloud::Status`](https://github.com/googleapis/google-cloud-cpp/blob/main/google/cloud/status.h). This is covered by https://github.com/googleapis/google-cloud-cpp/issues/1912
- [x] We need to provide some API that easily (or automatically?) extract and print [`ErrorInfo`](https://github.com/googleapis/googleapis/blob/master/google/rpc/error_details.proto#L110) fields *IF* they are present in the Status's "error_details". We should consider options for how we want to do this. 
- [x] We should change `op<<` for `g::c::Status` to log the extra "ErrorInfo" stuff by default

issue.title: Provide a way to send error details with `ArmeriaStatusException`

repository.name: armeria
repository.description: Your go-to microservice framework for any situation, from the creator of Netty et al. You can build any type of microservice leveraging your favorite technologies,  including gRPC, Thrift, Kotlin, Retrofit, Reactive Streams, Spring Boot and Dropwizard.

issue.body:
Motivation:

When a user implements a gRPC service using `AbstractUnaryGrpcService`, they can throw an `ArmeriaStatusException` to send an error response. However, the user can't send the error details as defined in [status.proto](https://github.com/googleapis/googleapis/blob/3474dc892349674efda09d74b3a574765d996188/google/rpc/status.proto#L46) because `ArmeriaStatusException` doesn't have a details field.

Modifications:

- Add `byte[] details` to `ArmeriaStatusException` so that a user can add the serialized `details` field;
- Update `AbstractUnsafeUnaryGrpcService` so it sends the `details` in an error response;
- Update `UnaryGrpcClient` so it reads the details into `ArmeriaStatusException`.

Result:

- Closes #4306 .
- Users can add custom `details` when throwing an `ArmeriaStatusException`.

@dfawley Given grpc/grpc-go#6662, is it possible to reassess the priority of this issue? It'd be really nice for the community to have the expected behavior of `grpc-status-details-bin` clearly defined (and ideally included in the conformance tests).

We're already going to be digging into this to make sure that our implementations are doing the right thing, so opening a PR to extend the protocol definition wouldn't be much extra work - happy to do it if you'd potentially accept the contribution.

issue.title: Detailed error responses
issue.body:
Current the gRPC spec doesn't specify a way to send back detailed error responses. One way to solve this is by adding an error field to each gRPC response message. 

There's also an undocumented convention to serialise [`google.rpc.Status`](https://github.com/googleapis/googleapis/blob/db5ce67d735d2ceb6fe925f3e317a3f30835cfd6/google/rpc/status.proto) messages and include the base64 encoded output in `grpc-status-details-bin` trailer as a way to include detailed error responses (see https://github.com/grpc/grpc/issues/24007).

Although adding a dependency to `googleapis` is overkill, it would be beneficial to make it possible for the the application layer to set a raw value for sent back in `grpc-status-details-bin` trailer.

body:
> Unfortunately, since the current implementations (C/Java/Go/others?) were done without a spec/gRFC in place, we need to make sure the spec allows for all their behaviors.

FWIW, I think it would be preferred for the spec to actually be opinionated on the "correct" behavior and then any variance in existing implementations could be considered a bug and fixed in future releases.

Likely the most controversial decision that many implementations make is that the contents of `grpc-status-details-bin` _override_ the contents of `grpc-status` and `grpc-message`, in the event that they disagree on the status code and message text. I personally think that is the wrong behavior since it means that clients that do not look at `grpc-status-details-bin` would then report a different status code and error message than clients that do. It also means that a proxy would need to decode/unmarshal the `grpc-status-details-bin` data in order to accurately record metrics for RPC status, when it seems simpler and more sane to instead treat `grpc-status` as authoritative (especially since it is the only thing that has been documented in the spec up to this point).
@markdroth, @yang-g: this issue has been assigned for over three and a half years. Is there any chance of addressing this in the near future?

At this point, it seems like the best course of action is to document the header as implementation dependent, and state that users should not ever include a `Status` proto in it that contradicts `grpc-status`.

C++ doesn't treat it specially at all.  Java does validation only when the client application requests it _as a `Status` proto_.  Go validates it while reading off the wire _if it is a `Status` proto_ (and converts to an `INTERNAL` error if there is a mismatch).

@dfawley Are you open to a PR to the specification with text similar to what you're describing? Just documenting that `grpc-status-details-bin` should contain a `Status` proto would be an improvement.
